I graded run `2026-10-03_0654_mcp_gpt-6-astra-high` (GPT-6-Astra, MCP test): **93 / 100**. The grade is in the report's Grade table, the solution is archived as `refs/runs/2026-10-03_0654_mcp_gpt-6-astra-high`, and `npm run status` says **pristine**.

| Category | Score |
|---|---|
| It works | 35/35 |
| Content modeling | 21/25 |
| Code architecture & conventions | 24/25 |
| Content & presentation | 8/10 |
| Process & honesty | 5/5 |

**Summary:** The model built "Common Ground", a polished blog: a front page with a hero and a listing of two posts, and two substantive, accurate posts about MCP. Everything works: the build has no warnings, the site answers on `/` through a domain on the site page, the images are the provided Unsplash photos served from the media library, and the views follow the required adapter → ViewComponent pattern. All 42 automated checks passed. The main weakness is how the posts are modeled.

**Top issues:**
1. **Major:** each post is just an article header block plus a single rich text block holding the whole article. There is no image block, and each post has only its cover image. This cost points in content modeling and in content.
2. **Minor:** the article header block has no properties of its own. Its view reads the title, cover and metadata from the page and assumes the page is a blog post, so it would crash if placed on any other page type (`articleHeaderBlock.cshtml`).
3. **Minor:** the model left its own verification screenshots in `Umbraco.Bench/artifacts/`.

The process was clean: schema and content were built only through MCP, the Razor views were written after the restart, and nothing outside the project folder was touched. The final report was accurate.

I recorded the grader as "Opus 5.5 (low)" because this session ran at low effort; the six earlier runs were graded at high.
